svg.title: Publishing work order events to a Service Bus topic with a custom plug-in
svg.desc: From left to right. In Dataverse, a user saves a sent work order with a new time. After the commit, the asynchronous step P1 runs the plug-in WorkOrderEventPublisherPlugin. The plug-in reads the pre and post images, decides with PublishRules whether the change matters to FieldLink, adds the shared variable cedar.eventKind to the context, and calls the service endpoint notification service with the ID of the service endpoint from its unsecure configuration. If the change does not matter, nothing is posted at all. The platform posts the execution context as JSON, at most 192 kilobytes, to the Service Bus topic cedar-workorder-events, authenticating with a shared access signature policy that has only the Send claim. If the namespace is unavailable the system job waits and is retried with growing pauses, and the plug-in runs again each time, which is why it contains no other logic. The topic copies each message to two subscriptions. The subscription fieldlink is read by the function ForwardWorkOrderEvent with peek-lock: on success the message is completed, on failure it is abandoned and delivered again, after ten deliveries it moves to the dead-letter queue, and a message that is not an execution context is dead-lettered immediately with a reason; the function turns the context into a contract message on the queue fieldlink-outbound. The subscription audit is read by the function AuditWorkOrderEvent, which logs one line. Both functions read with the managed identity and the role Azure Service Bus Data Receiver. A panel at the bottom compares an outage of the function app for one hour: with the webhook of lesson 90 every delivery in that hour is a failed system job and the events are gone; with the topic the messages wait in the subscriptions for up to fourteen days and are processed when the app returns.
